library_preparation_preflight.summary: jakarta.xml.ws-api is a spec-only jar. Service.create, Endpoint.create/publish and the other main entry points call Provider.provider(), which looks up a jakarta.xml.ws.spi.Provider through ServiceLoader. Without a runtime, tests can only reach exceptions, enums, annotations and similar. I did not run anything against the artifact. This rests on the API's known design and on the repo's existing jaxws-rt test.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Write tests against the jakarta.xml.ws API only: Service.create(QName), Endpoint.create(...), the BindingProvider request/response context, Dispatch, handler chains, WebServiceFeature classes such as AddressingFeature, MTOMFeature and RespectBindingFeature, EndpointReference and W3CEndpointReferenceBuilder, and the WebServiceException hierarchy. Do not import com.sun.xml.ws.* classes in the tests, so coverage is attributed to the API. Do not use Docker or external network services. Publish endpoints on the JDK's built-in HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 with port 0 or a free port, or use local WSDL resources for Service.create. No environment variables or system properties are required. Provider discovery should work through the ServiceLoader META-INF/services entry. If it does not, set the system property jakarta.xml.ws.spi.Provider to com.sun.xml.ws.spi.ProviderImpl.
risks: The runtime uses reflection, JAXB and SOAP, so native-image runs may need extra reachability metadata for jaxws-rt classes. Expect to iterate with the metadata generation and fix tasks.
Endpoint.publish needs the JDK's com.sun.net.httpserver, or the jaxws-rt HTTP transport. Choose ports carefully to avoid flakiness.
The jaxws-rt 4.0.5 dependency tree may bring a newer jakarta.xml.ws-api than 4.0.3. Make sure the tested artifact is the one under test.
